title: Gideon and the Undertow
premise: Jonah Ravensworth has spent fifteen years writing postcards to their childhood home—an address that burned down the year their brother Gideon disappeared—cataloguing everything the family never said. When the land beneath the ruin goes up at auction, Jonah must return to the coastal town that arranged itself around a silence: everyone quietly agrees Gideon drowned, though no body was ever found. As bidding begins, Jonah uncovers evidence that Gideon ran, and that their father's will—the inheritance binding them all—was built on that lie. In the end, Jonah chooses to let the house sell, reads one last postcard aloud at the auction, and finally receives an answer: a postcard from Gideon, alive, asking to be found.
about_author: Ada Thornbury is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who left practice after a decade of administering wills built on family silences. They write from a rented cottage on the Atlantic coast, where they keep, they admit, a careful inventory of everything unsaid.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet Jonah in their city apartment, writing the four-hundredth postcard to a burned address, filing each unsent confession in a shoebox. The beat: meticulous loneliness disguised as ritual.

chapters.title: Notice of Sale
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A lawyer's letter arrives: the Ravensworth lot is up for auction in six weeks, and all heirs must consent or contest. Jonah realizes someone else wants the land. Beat: dread dressed as paperwork.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback, young Jonah's POV. The night of the fire and Gideon's disappearance—Jonah saw something from the dunes but told no one. Beat: guilt as origin story.

chapters.title: The Town That Agreed
chapters.summary: Jonah returns to Marrow Cove; old neighbors greet them with rehearsed kindness, everyone performing the same grief. Beat: the suffocating warmth of complicity.

chapters.title: Aunt Vera's Good China
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. The aunt who raised the alibi polishes china for an auction-day reception, revealing she knows more about the fire than she says. Beat: hospitality as armor.

chapters.title: The Rival Bidder
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A developer named Cass Okafor is buying up the cove; Jonah assumes greed, but Cass asks oddly specific questions about the Ravensworths. Beat: suspicion with a human face.

chapters.title: Postcards, Returned
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the ruined mailbox, Jonah finds one of their own postcards—opened, annotated in handwriting they almost recognize. Beat: vertigo; the past answering back.

chapters.title: Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah breaks into the sealed boathouse and finds their father's ledger: payments, dates, and a column labeled only 'G.' Beat: the law's tidy justice beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Brother Halves
chapters.summary: Older sister Maren's POV. Maren, who stayed and became the town's nurse, confronts Jonah for coming back and stirring what everyone buried. Beat: love expressed as hostility.

chapters.title: The Auction Terms
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Reading the will's fine print, Jonah learns the sale requires unanimous heir consent—and one signature is forged. Beat: hope arriving through fraud.

chapters.title: Salt and Testimony
chapters.summary: Jonah interviews the retired harbormaster, whose drunk memory places Gideon on a boat the night of the fire. Beat: the first hard evidence he didn't drown.

chapters.title: Cass's Offer
chapters.summary: Cass reveals she was fostered briefly by the Ravensworths and saw Gideon alive weeks after the fire. She offers to split the land—if Jonah helps her find him. Beat: alliance born of mutual hunger.

chapters.title: Vera Breaks a Plate
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Jonah shows her the ledger; Vera shatters china and confesses Father paid her to swear the family was together that night. Beat: the alibi's architect crumbling.

chapters.title: Maren's Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Jonah searches Maren's clinic office and finds Gideon's school records, altered. Beat: betrayal inside the family's gentlest member.

chapters.title: The Fire Marshal's File
chapters.summary: Jonah pulls the arson report: accelerant used by someone with a key. Beat: the fire wasn't accident or escape—it was erasure.

chapters.title: Who Had a Key
chapters.summary: Jonah lists keyholders: Father, Vera, Maren, and—chillingly—Jonah themselves, whose key went missing that summer. Beat: suspicion turning inward.

chapters.title: A Night at the Dunes
chapters.summary: Jonah sleeps at the ruin and relives the memory fully: it was Maren's figure on the dunes, not Father's. Beat: memory revising itself against loyalty.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Clinic
chapters.summary: Jonah accuses Maren; she neither confirms nor denies, only says 'You were a child; you don't know what he was.' Beat: the possibility that Gideon was dangerous.

chapters.title: Gideon, Unreliable
chapters.summary: Recovered fragments—old letters, a teacher's note—paint Gideon as violent, manipulative, possibly the fire's author. Beat: sympathy for the missing curdles into fear.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Jonah traces the forged heir signature to Vera's hand—she signed for dead Grandmother Ruth to keep the sale blocked until now. Beat: protection revealed as control.

chapters.title: Cass's Ledger Too
chapters.summary: Jonah discovers Cass has been paying Vera for information; her search for Gideon isn't sentimental—she claims he owes her something terrible. Beat: ally or avenger?

chapters.title: Midsummer Meeting
chapters.summary: All heirs summoned to Vera's; Maren moves to approve the sale and end it forever. Jonah vetoes with the forged-signature evidence. Beat: open rupture at the family table.

chapters.title: The Shoebox Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Jonah burns through reading their own unsent postcards to Maren, confessing fifteen years of silence. Beat: catharsis without absolution.

chapters.title: What Jonah Saw, Corrected
chapters.summary: Under hypnosis-free honest retelling, Jonah admits they may have helped Gideon pack that night—memory suppressed to survive. Beat: complicity acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster Recants
chapters.summary: Pressured by someone, the harbormaster withdraws his statement. Beat: the town closing ranks again, now with threats.

chapters.title: Bricks Through Windows
chapters.summary: Anonymous intimidation escalates; Jonah's rental is vandalized with the word LIAR. Beat: justice outside the law turning mob-shaped.

chapters.title: Vera's Deathbed Dictation
chapters.summary: Vera, failing fast, dictates a letter: Father started the fire to destroy Gideon's crimes and fake his death; she kept the ledger to hold power over him. Beat: the patriarch unmasked posthumously.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Following Vera's letter, Jonah finds Father's private plot behind the church—empty except for Gideon's burned belongings, staged as remains. Beat: the drowning officially a fiction.

chapters.title: Maren Confesses
chapters.summary: Maren admits she saw Father set the fire and chose silence to protect Jonah from knowing what Gideon had done—to her. Beat: the reveal reframes every prior chapter.

chapters.title: Justice, Considered
chapters.summary: Jonah weighs reporting Father (dead), exposing Maren, finding Gideon. Cass demands they find him for her own reckoning. Beat: the ethics of digging.

chapters.title: The Annotated Postcard Traced
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis points to a man living under another name two towns north. Beat: the hunt narrowing to a door.

chapters.title: The Door in Ashford
chapters.summary: Jonah and Cass drive out; a man with Gideon's eyes answers but denies everything. Beat: recognition without reunion.

chapters.title: Cass's Claim
chapters.summary: Cass reveals Gideon defrauded her mother years ago; she wants restitution, not police. Beat: two wounded people negotiating what justice means.

chapters.title: Gideon Speaks
chapters.summary: Gideon finally talks: he lit nothing, but he took the money and let the family believe him dead because being dead was safer than being their son. Beat: the question the family arranged itself around, answered.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: The whole town gathers; Maren signs, Vera's proxy voided, the hammer falls—Cass wins the lot. Beat: public ending of a private era.

chapters.title: The Last Postcard
chapters.summary: At the auction's edge, Jonah reads aloud the final unsent postcard—a forgiveness, not an accusation. Beat: release witnessed by the town that conspired.

chapters.title: Terms of Belonging
chapters.summary: Jonah and Gideon meet properly; no reconciliation, but an agreement: truth over myth, contact without custody of the past. Beat: belonging redefined, not restored.

chapters.title: What Cass Builds
chapters.summary: Cass plans housing on the lot with a memorial garden where the house stood; Maren offers the clinic's records for the archive. Beat: the land repurposed toward honesty.

chapters.title: Emptying the Shoebox
chapters.summary: Jonah mails forty years of postcards—not to the burned address, but to living recipients, each unsaid thing finally said. Beat: the inventory closed.

chapters.title: Undertow, Ebbing
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Jonah's POV on the dunes at dawn: a new postcard arrives—from Gideon, addressed properly this time, asking a small ordinary question. Jonah writes back the same day. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
